claims.statement: PDCAT improves acceleration performance over GCC default -O3 optimization setting on all selected cases at 5,000 seconds.
claims.evidence_quote: PDCAT achieves 5.5%-81.2% acceleration performance over GCC default -O3 optimization setting in all 28 selected cases in 5,000 seconds.

claims.statement: PDCAT significantly outperforms four compared compiler auto-tuning techniques, including the state-of-the-art technique SRTuner.
claims.evidence_quote: PDCAT significantly outperforms the four compared techniques, including the state-of-art technique SRTuner.

claims.statement: PDCAT achieves the best optimization result on 10/11/14 programs at 1,250/2,500/5,000 seconds, while RIO, CFSCA, CompTuner and SRTuner achieve best results on only 2/1/1, 5/3/2, 3/5/4 and 8/8/7 programs, respectively.
claims.evidence_quote: PDCAT achieves the best optimization result on 10/11/14 programs in 1,250/2,500/5,000 seconds, while the compared RIO, CFSCA, CompTuner and SRTuner achieve the best results on only 2/1/1, 5/3/2, 3/5/4 and 8/8/7, respectively.

claims.statement: PDCAT never achieves the worst result on 28 programs at 1,250/2,500/5,000 seconds, whereas baselines achieve worst results in multiple cases.
claims.evidence_quote: PDCAT never achieves the worst results on 28 programs in 1,250/2,500/5,000 seconds, while the compared RIO, CFSCA, CompTuner and SRTuner achieve the worst results in 18/18/21, 3/3/3, 6/5/3 and 1/2/1, respectively.

claims.statement: SPDCAT replaces PDCAT's myopic, high-variance preference update with a random-forest surrogate that uses UCB acquisition and smoothed marginal-effect preference updates.
claims.evidence_quote: We propose SPDCAT, which keeps PDCAT's preference-driven space reduction but replaces the myopic update with a random-forest surrogate used in two coupled roles: an upper-confidence-bound acquisition function selects the next configuration, and a surrogate-informed preference update refines each flag's enable probability from smoothed marginal-effect estimates.

claims.statement: On PolyBench (GCC 11.4.0), SPDCAT attains a higher median speedup over -O3 than PDCAT and RIO under equal time budgets, winning 7 of 10 programs and significantly beating RIO (p=0.037).
claims.evidence_quote: SPDCAT attains a higher median speedup over \texttt{-O3} than both PDCAT and the RIO random baseline under equal time budgets---winning 7 of 10 programs and significantly beating RIO ($p=0.037$)---with the largest gains where tuning headroom exists.

claims.statement: SPDCAT has the largest advantage where tuning headroom exists, with gemm at +49.4% speedup over -O3 vs +42.3% for PDCAT and +37.0% for RIO.
At the largest budget (360s), SPDCAT opens a clear gap over PDCAT and RIO, with mean speedup over -O3 of -2.3% for SPDCAT, -4.5% for PDCAT, and -11.1% for RIO.
Ablation study confirms that both UCB selection and the surrogate-informed preference update contribute to SPDCAT's performance.
claims.evidence_quote: An ablation study confirms that the UCB selection and the preference update each contribute.

agent.overall_conclusion: SPDCAT retains PDCAT's preference-driven space reduction but replaces its myopic search step with a random-forest surrogate using UCB acquisition and smoothed marginal-effect updates. On PolyBench (GCC 11.4.0), SPDCAT achieves a higher median speedup over -O3 than PDCAT and RIO, winning 7 of 10 programs and significantly beating RIO (p=0.037), with the largest gains on gemm (+49.4% vs +42.3% for PDCAT and +37.0% for RIO). At 360s, mean speedup over -O3 is -2.3% for SPDCAT, -4.5% for PDCAT, and -11.1% for RIO.
